objective: Construct an executable nondestructive noise-identification experiment for valid quantum codes: extract every statistically identifiable combination of specified noise-mixture weights while returning the arbitrary unknown logical state unchanged. Output the measurement instrument, predicted observation model, identifiability certificate and estimator. This is a different productive objective from recovering a corrupted logical state.
beneficiary: MONTREAL.AI internal computational quantum-code/noise research. CPU simulation and mathematical protocol construction only; no physical hardware, fault-tolerance, world novelty or revenue claim.
deliverable: Self-contained Python module noise_experiment.py exporting class NoiseExperiment. Standard library, NumPy and SciPy permitted. Independently supplied prior assets may be used only when present in the assigned workspace. The same read-only primary-source and web-documentation research is permitted in every arm. No cross-arm or private verification files, downloads, additional packages, paid services or execution-time network dependence.

inputs.constructor: NoiseExperiment(n: int, codewords: list[dict[int, complex]], hypotheses: list[dict])
inputs.codewords: Ordered orthonormal K=2 logical basis in integer-coordinate sparse complex form, qubit0 most-significant bit. Codes satisfy correction of arbitrary errors on any one qubit. Qualified finite domain n<=9, <=2048 total code amplitudes, well-conditioned exact-code families.
inputs.hypotheses: Each dictionary has name (unique string), qubit (integer physical position), and kraus (nonempty list of complex 2x2 matrices). Each is a known local CPTP channel. Unknown nonnegative mixture weights sum to one. Up to32 hypotheses. Duplicate or intrinsically indistinguishable hypotheses are valid and must not be falsely called identifiable.

interface.measurement_operators: measurement_operators() -> list of outcome operators. Each outcome operator consists of K sparse dictionaries giving direct row coefficients: output[row]=sum(coefficient[word]*input[word]). Each registered outcome has one Kraus operator, maps physical input to the recovered logical space, and is an executable measurement branch. Export finite operators, not only an abstract information score.
interface.response_matrix: response_matrix() -> real LxH matrix A. A[o,h] is the probability of registered outcome o under hypothesis h, independent of the unknown logical input. Rows match measurement_operators() exactly; columns match hypothesis order. The erasure flag has zero probability for these supported noise hypotheses and is excluded from A.
interface.identifiability: identifiability() -> dict {rank: int, unique: bool, identifiable_projector: real HxH array}. Projector is the orthogonal Euclidean projector onto row(A). unique is true exactly when rank==H. Its nullspace describes genuinely unidentifiable changes in mixture weights; normalization is included in the row space.
interface.estimate: estimate(observed: real length-L vector of nonnegative counts or probabilities with positive sum) -> dict {mixture_weights: real length-H probability vector, identifiable_coordinates: real length-H vector, predicted_frequencies: real length-L vector, unique: bool}. Normalize this classical count vector explicitly. For nonidentifiable models, mixture_weights is a feasible representative, not a claim of a unique underlying mixture; identifiable_coordinates equals identifiable_projector@mixture_weights and predicted_frequencies equals A@mixture_weights. Reject zero total observations.

acceptance.nondisturbance: For each supported hypothesis and every logical input, each measurement branch is proportional to that same logical state. The unconditional sum returns the original logical density with no postselection; observed probabilities cannot depend on the logical state. Verify on the full Pauli-correctable span, not only one logical probe.
acceptance.complete_instrument: Let S be the span of all single-qubit I,X,Y,Z images of the code. The measurement operators satisfy sum M_o^dagger M_o=projector(S). Outside S, an additional classical erasure outcome completes the channel and preserves total raw mass. The logical output and erasure form a CPTP instrument, including subnormalized inputs.
acceptance.maximal_identifiability: A must attain the linear rank available in the physical output density operators of the specified noise hypotheses acting on a fixed encoded pure logical state. Correctability makes that available noise information independent of which logical state is used. Do not assert distinguishability that the code/channel physics removes. No optimal-shot-complexity or globally optimal experimental-design claim is required.
acceptance.ideal_probabilities_primary: On fresh mixtures, noiseless model probabilities must yield the correct identifiable coordinates and predicted observations, with a feasible normalized mixture representative. In full-rank cases recover the actual weights. In deficient-rank cases report unique=false and reproduce the identifiable quotient; never invent distinguishability.
acceptance.finite_counts_secondary: Run fresh seeded multinomial observations and record estimator errors, fitted probabilities and statistical limitations. These secondary observations are descriptive finite-sample results, not a universal accuracy guarantee and not grounds to alter the primary pass decision.
acceptance.tolerances: Physical/operator/response/certificate error <=2e-8 in scale-appropriate entrywise or spectral norms. Ideal-probability estimator error <=2e-6. Rank decisions are evaluated on finite cases with a separated nonzero singular spectrum.
acceptance.resources: CPU only, at most10GiB process memory; ordinary isolated scientific-Python subprocess, not Forge seccomp. Efficient sparse, active-coordinate or modest dense conventional calculations are allowed within that same budget.

cases.purpose: Nonorthogonal full-rank noise model; all mixture weights are physically identifiable.
Degenerate model; identify the available quotient and honestly report nonuniqueness.

procedure.construction: Fresh isolated-in-context constructor, one initial source plus at most two development repairs. Freeze source before private qualification; preserve every submission and failure. No private results may drive same-experiment repair.
procedure.withheld: Fresh code variants, noise libraries, logical probes, mixture weights and observations are independently frozen before first submission. Separate verifier agent does not inspect constructed source.
procedure.comparison: Matched fresh included-agent constructions with and without the retained first capability, plus competent ordinary reconstruction/reuse. Same public objective, information, tools, resource envelope and acceptance. Do not weaken the conventional comparator.
procedure.accounting: Record actual construction interval, source hashes, tool/process receipts, failed attempts, acquisition, integration, qualification and execution. First-capability cost is retained in cumulative comparisons; unknown model inference or monetary costs remain unknown.
procedure.claims: A qualified distinct experiment is required before any transfer conclusion. Repeated measured construction savings may support a bounded transfer observation, not an improved-inventor, general causal, monetization or full economic-compounding claim.
